title: Safety of Umbilical Cord Stem Cells Given by IV or Spinal Injection in Adults With Probable Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE)
official: A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Dose-Escalation Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Exploratory Activity of Intravenous and Intrathecal Administration of XytriX (Allogeneic Human Umbilical Cord Tissue-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells) in Adults With Probable Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE)
summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of intravenous and intrathecal XytriX™ (umbilical-derived mesenchymal stem cells) in adults with confirmed or probable CTE, characterizing the incidence, frequency, and severity of TEAEs, SAEs, and any adverse events leading to withdrawal, over 24 months. The investigators also aim to study the preliminary efficacy of XytriX™ as measured by changes from baseline in neurocognitive function, behavioral/psychiatric symptoms, functional status, and biomarker profiles through 24 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Age 18 years or older, any sex.

* Documented history of repetitive traumatic brain injury (rTBI): defined as ≥2 concussive events documented by medical record, AND/OR confirmed history of exposure to explosive blast (military), AND/OR ≥10 years of participation in contact sport with documented head trauma.
* Presence of at least 2 of the following CTE-consistent clinical symptoms for ≥6 months: cognitive impairment (memory, attention, executive dysfunction); behavioral dysregulation (aggression, impulsivity); mood disorder (depression, anxiety); or progressive functional decline not explained by other causes.
* Supported by at least one of the following Supportive Features under the published CTE biomarker literature: (i) plasma NfL above age-adjusted 97.5th percentile (Simoa HD-X); (ii) plasma GFAP above age-adjusted 75th percentile (Simoa HD-X); (iii) plasma p-tau181 above age-adjusted upper reference limit (Simoa HD-X); or (iv) formal TES diagnosis of CTE Possible or CTE Probable by a board-certified neurologist applying the NINDS Traumatic Encephalopathy Syndrome (TES) Criteria (Katz et al., Neurology 2021).
* MoCA score ≥18 at screening (mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment range; sufficient for informed consent and outcome assessment).
* Willing and able to provide written informed consent, or a legally authorized representative is willing to consent.
* Willingness to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits for 24 months.
* Women of childbearing potential: negative urine pregnancy test prior to each treatment; agreement to use effective contraception through 6 months post-last treatment.
* Caregiver or study partner available for behavioral/functional assessments.

Exclusion Criteria:

Exclusion Criteria

Subjects meeting ANY of the following criteria will be excluded:

* Confirmed diagnosis of other neurodegenerative disease as primary etiology (Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, frontotemporal dementia, Lewy body dementia, or ALS).
* Active malignancy or treatment for cancer within the past 2 years (except basal cell carcinoma).
* Active systemic infection, including HIV or active hepatitis B/C.
* Immunocompromised state or current immunosuppressive therapy.
* Organ transplant history.
* MoCA score \<18 at screening.
* Current or recent (within 30 days) participation in another interventional clinical trial.
* History of hypersensitivity or adverse reaction to DMSO or stem cell therapies.
* Significant active cerebrovascular disease (large territory stroke, AVM, or uncontrolled CNS vasculopathy) that could confound neurological outcomes.
* Active psychosis requiring hospitalization or posing safety risk.
* Active suicidal ideation with specific plan or intent at screening (C-SSRS high-risk categories).
* Conditions that would preclude reliable biomarker sample collection or neurocognitive testing.
* For Cohort 3 (IT) specifically: coagulopathy or anticoagulation that cannot be safely bridged; severe degenerative disc disease preventing safe LP; spinal cord compression or mass lesion.
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
* Medical condition that would, in the opinion of the PI, compromise patient safety or ability to comply with study procedures.
